biggestGap: The pith collar is a STROKED OUTLINE, not a torn edge: frozen `spokes` on the outer annulus (scale=0.95 r0=0.80 r1=1.00, matched face windows) puts the band's fine angular texture at ang_energy_hi 21.01 -> 19.27 landscape and 22.06 -> 17.40 portrait against a scale-matched plate-01's 40.59 / 36.90 — barely half, and FALLING this round — because `capCoords` fades its radius warp to zero above r0 0.90 (`ss(0.90,0.70,r0)`) and `collarTilt` is a pure function of `rad`, so the band is by construction a constant-width, texture-free cream arc with two hard boundaries where the reference has a ragged pith zone that red fibre fingers invade.

THE_MEASUREMENT_AND_WHY_IT_SURVIVES_THE_.command: python3 tools/probes.py spokes <png> win=<matched face window> scale=0.95 r0=0.80 r1=1.00 — one frozen probe, three documented kwargs, identical on every side, mask_px printed. r0/r1 restrict the polar sampling to the outer 20% of the cap ellipse, which IS the collar band; `spokes` removes each ring's own mean, so the radial brightness profile we just fixed contributes nothing and only ANGULAR structure survives.
THE_MEASUREMENT_AND_WHY_IT_SURVIVES_THE_.THE_A_FORTIORI_THAT_MAKES_IT_SAFE: Every other collar statistic I tried moves 2-3x on the plate under pure Lanczos resample, so I chose the one where the resample HURTS THE REFERENCE: downsampling strips fine angular energy, and plate-405's collar annulus — a region 31% SMALLER than our landscape one (3327 px vs 4837) and downsampled 4.1x — still carries 1.9x our fine energy. There is no region-size or resolution story that produces this sign. It is also the only collar number that agrees across three independent controls: ours sits at 47% of plate-640 and 47% of plate-405.
THE_MEASUREMENT_AND_WHY_IT_SURVIVES_THE_.the_mechanism_named_in_the_file_itself: src/fruit/species.js:1346-1349, `capCoords`: `const warp = fbm2(...).mul(ss(0.90, 0.70, r0))`. The comment above it is round 3's and its reasoning is CORRECT — 'the band is 0.052 wide in rad and the untapered warp displaced rad by up to +-0.055, so a spoke could be pushed clean past it ... Warp the flesh, leave the shell alone.' Round 3 was right that a RADIAL DISPLACEMENT of a 0.05-wide band is the wrong lever. But that argument was then read as 'do not touch the collar at all', and the consequence is `collarTilt` (species.js:1298-1302), three smoothsteps in `rad` and nothing else, plus a pith albedo with no field on it. The band therefore has EXACTLY the same width, the same brightness envelope and the same two hard boundaries at every one of the 180 rays. That is the definition of a drawn ring.
THE_MEASUREMENT_AND_WHY_IT_SURVIVES_THE_.the_picture_says_the_same_thing_at_12x: /tmp/r9_edge12.png (landscape, 60x65 px at 12x NEAREST) against /tmp/p640_edge12.png (plate-640, identical crop size and magnification). Ours: a smooth cream arc ~3.5 px wide, near-uniform in value, hard against the red on the inside and hard against the green on the outside, running the full arc without a break. Plate-640: a broad, ragged, VARIABLE-width pale zone with red fibre fingers pushing out into it and pale tissue pushing back into the green, no boundary you could trace with a pen. Portrait (/tmp/r9p_edge12.png) is worse, and that is what the 17.40 says.
THE_MEASUREMENT_AND_WHY_IT_SURVIVES_THE_.why_this_is_a_STILL_failure_and_not_a_mo: This is the right question for the 80 boundary and this is the honest answer. In motion a smooth bright arc at a cut edge is indistinguishable from a wet rim highlight — it is exactly what a specular rim DOES look like at 30 px/frame, and nobody resolves 3 px of texture on it. Frozen, a boundary of constant width and constant value is the oldest CG tell there is: real tissue has no constant anything. Everything else on this axis now survives a still — the mean level (172.8 against plate-640's 188.6 face), the chroma (0.3675 against 0.3190), the radial profile's sign, the three-layer stack, the boundary smoothness. Handed the two crops unlabelled at matched pixel size (/tmp/blind_A.png = plate, /tmp/blind_B.png = r9, both 8x, face major axis matched) I still pick the render instantly, but now on ONE thing — surface texture — where in r8 I picked it on level, chroma, profile AND texture. That is the +4.

evidence.WHAT_I_CHECKED_AND_FOUND_NOTHING_WRONG_W: (i) I instrumented `collar`'s own ridge-peak locations and drew them (/tmp/ridge_r9.png, /tmp/ridge_p640.png). On our frame the 177 peaks form a clean connected ring at the flesh/pith join — the probe IS finding the collar, its region is right, and ridge_t_med 0.629 is a true statistic. On plate-640 the 179 peaks scatter over the whole face because the plate has no annulus that outshines its own interior. That difference is real and it is the same finding as the headline, but `ridge_t_cv` cannot express it (ours 0.213 vs plate-640's 0.231) so I did not build a claim on it. fix: One file, src/fruit/species.js, and do NOT spend it on level, chroma or the radial ramp — all three are now at or near the scale-matched plate and every round that has re-spent them has netted zero. Give the collar band a torn EDGE, and take the edge modulation TANGENTIALLY, not radially. Round 3's comment at species.js:1340-1345 is correct and I am not asking anyone to undo it: bodily displacing a 0.052-wide band by +-0.055 in `rad` makes the shell vanish on some spokes, which is why `capCoords` fades its warp with `ss(0.90,0.70,r0)`. But 'do not displace the band' was then read as 'do not vary the band', and the result is `collarTilt` (species.js:1298-1302) — three smoothsteps in `rad` and nothing else — so the band has identical width, identical envelope and two hard boundaries at all 180 rays. (1) THE EDGES, NOT THE POSITION. Perturb the INNER threshold of the pith wall and the inner edge of the pith albedo by a low-amplitude field sampled in `cc.q` (cartesian — NOT `cc.ang`, which is the seam-at-+-PI and spoke problem the file already knows about at :1300), amplitude ~0.4x the band width so the boundary frays and the flesh interdigitates with the pith, while the band's CENTRE `rad` and its outer edge against the peel stay exactly where they are. Keep `collarTilt`'s area-weighted mean fixed so no shading budget moves. (2) LET THE WET FILM ONTO THE BAND. `wetField`'s `lig` is gated by `ss(0.25,0.92,cc.rad)`, i.e. it is faded OUT across exactly the annulus that needs it, and the foam blobs are additionally gated by `blobFade` at that pixel size; the plate's pith zone is the WETTEST part of its face (R1: 'a bright wet rim where flesh meets rind'). Move the gate's upper edge out past 1.0 so the band keeps its film. (3) Same treatment for the citrus, where there is no pale band at all to fray yet — the orange needs a pith albedo before it needs an edge.
